N2.subject: Authorization, review and ASR as optional draft
N2.judgment: Supported and ethically qualified; no legal or product-enforcement claim. Legacy ambiguity and human/index alternatives remain explicit.

N2.subject: Whisper defaults, units and model limitations
N2.judgment: Pinned implementation and card support the stated booleans/seconds and limitations. The dependency of silence handling on word timestamps is omitted from the compressed final, but no contrary usage prescription is made.

N2.subject: Whisper issue→fix→release chain
N2.judgment: Specific #1046→#1052→v20230307 chain is supported. Final denies a universal fix. Source-note later-history drift is minor and separately recorded.

N2.subject: Editable timed multilingual data, translation and OHD upload limits
N2.judgment: Structured revision requirements are recommendations; documented OHD editing and per-file uploads support the optional route. Export fidelity remains proposed validation.

N2.subject: Search units, language/access filters, passage navigation and public-access boundary
N2.judgment: Rights-aware search is necessary for this brief; a database index remains viable. OHD's registered/archive-granted comparator is not sold as anonymous public search.

N2.subject: Mukurtu defaults and content/media divergence
N2.judgment: All/Any, default All, and distinct item/media settings are source-supported. No inference of arbitrary within-file controls.

N2.subject: Mukurtu dependencies, private path and maturity
N2.judgment: Deployment facts supported; final correctly leaves code maturity open and limits development status to the manual. Historical discovery/source-note error is not retained as final advice.

N2.subject: OHMS Viewer media/XML separation and cache rule
N2.judgment: Supported limited cache-HTTP protection, installation dependence, separate media hosting and historical-runtime qualification.

N2.subject: Segment restrictions and fallback
N2.judgment: Policy requirement is distinguished from unverified product capability. Redacted/split access media plus matching text/index or nonpublication is a technically plausible conditional mechanism, not tested security.

N2.subject: Withdrawal limits and master disposition
N2.judgment: Archive-controlled takedown is separated from external copies; retention/destruction depends on agreements and policy, not a guessed universal rule.

N2.subject: Source audio, fixity, replicas, BagIt and PREMIS
N2.judgment: Preservation/access distinction and limits of metadata/packaging are sound. No format standard is substituted for backups or access control; source format remains an inventory question.

N2.subject: Multilingual acceptance and human fallback
N2.judgment: Disaggregated language/condition evaluation is appropriate. Thresholds and reference availability are acknowledged decisions, not asserted accuracy results.

N2.subject: Conditional product alternatives and version drift
N2.judgment: OHD 1.4.1 versus v2.11.0 is independently confirmed without claiming hosted build identity. Mukurtu/OHD/OHMS/human/ASR routes remain conditional, not proven cheapest or a selected winner.

N2.subject: Privacy-aware names, metadata, translations and snippets
N2.judgment: Release review and controlled identities preserve the public catalog option while addressing disclosures. These are sensible requirements informed by ethics, not automatically available product guarantees.

N2.subject: Executed versus proposed validation and low-cost decision
N2.judgment: Only source review is claimed executed. Budget/staff/restore/access criteria and seven pilot groups are discriminating; no price, performance, security or restore result is invented.

N1.subject: OHMS self-host and managed Aviary alternatives
N1.judgment: Conditional oral-history routes are viable research leads. Viewer integration is independently supported; creator's application announcement supports investigating self-hosting without proving a current deployment.

N1.subject: Aviary editing, speakers, legacy conversion and time units
N1.judgment: Documented word/speaker/start-time editing, HH:MM:SS entry and millisecond-bearing WebVTT are supported. Legacy conversion/fidelity remains a test, not a lossless promise.

N1.subject: Aviary object permissions and uploaded-media assertions
N1.judgment: Statuses and vendor upload-security claims are correctly distinguished from audited security and per-segment ACLs.

N1.subject: Aviary pricing and one-pass calculation
N1.judgment: Displayed rates/caps support 120,000 minutes × $0.04 = $4,800 for one processing pass. It is not a combined transcription/translation/alignment bill or quote; billing period/storage/total cost remain open.

N1.subject: Mukurtu object protocols and All/Any
N1.judgment: Supported asset-level defaults and public-item/private-media possibility. Final specifically avoids presenting this as a synchronized transcript or segment-redaction product.

N1.subject: Omeka catalog, media privacy and role scopes
N1.judgment: Supported item/media and global/site-role distinctions; additional oral-history layer is explicitly needed.

N1.subject: Whisper training, language variation, hallucination, diarization and English translation
N1.judgment: Card/paper support the substantive cautions. Spoken-name transcription is distinguished from identity inference. Family translation capability is valid; turbo's translation exception is a model-selection limit, not a false claim that a selected model translates.

N1.subject: Whisper code evolution
N1.judgment: Security/device/documentation changes are present in v20250625. Timestamp improvement exists in cumulative history under v20230918. Final's file-level wording is defensible; its S14 note/locator blurs release attribution (minor).

N1.subject: OHMS subsecond conversion and index mapping
N1.judgment: Exact pinned symbols confirm dropped fractions, whole-second paths, integer comparison, half-open boundaries and first-match break. Static behavior is not mislabeled runtime execution.

N1.subject: OHMS navigation, legacy PDF and cache release trail
N1.judgment: Primary release notes support this relevant evolution sequence; cache protection is a configured path boundary and the navigation change does not prove millisecond precision.

N1.subject: ASR identities and source-language/translation separation
N1.judgment: Appropriate narrower identity safeguard retains ordinary spoken names subject to review. Translation is a derived output, not replacement source-language text.

N1.subject: Segment policy, redacted derivatives, withdrawal and consent/copyright
N1.judgment: Requirements are not inferred product capabilities. Agreements govern preservation disposition; downloaded public copies cannot be recalled. Prior versions and derivatives remain under rights controls.

N1.subject: BWF/LC applicability and original received bits
N1.judgment: The analog reformatting/native-resolution context is accurately qualified; no universal conversion mandate is inferred.

N1.subject: BagIt and PREMIS scope
N1.judgment: Packaging/fixity and preservation metadata are useful optional mechanisms; replication, permissions and restores are distinct work.

N1.subject: Capacity arithmetic
N1.judgment: Independently recomputed decimal results are correct: 4.1472 TB at 96k/24/stereo, 2.0736 TB at 48k/24/stereo, 57.6 GB at 64 kbit/s for 2,000 h. Assumptions/exclusions are explicit; no measured inventory or benchmark.

N1.subject: Language/condition protocol and operational validation
N1.judgment: Fluent references, script-sensitive WER/CER, disaggregation, feasible coverage and human fallback discriminate ASR usefulness. Source-timing fixtures, rights history, negative access, byte corruption and restore tests are proposed only.
